title: Human-centered values and fairness
text: AI should respect human rights, democratic values, and fairness. Consider impacts on individuals and society, especially in high-impact contexts. Use this as a cross-jurisdiction baseline to interpret governance expectations and justify safeguards.

title: Transparency and responsible disclosure
text: Provide meaningful information about AI systems to foster understanding and appropriate use. Disclose limitations, uncertainty, and intended purpose to prevent misuse and overreliance. Treat transparency as a governance control that improves explainability and trust.

title: Robustness, security, and safety across lifecycle
text: AI systems should be robust, secure, and safe throughout their lifecycle, including resilience against attacks. Implement monitoring and incident response so harms can be detected and managed. Robustness evidence supports explainable claims of safety.

title: Accountability for AI outcomes
text: AI actors should be accountable for proper functioning and for addressing adverse impacts. Assign owners and create escalation paths that can halt or modify deployments. Accountability is a governance property that must be demonstrable through artifacts and logs.

title: Risk management and monitoring appropriate to context
text: Adopt risk management and ongoing monitoring appropriate to context and impact of AI systems. Define control coverage, gaps, and improvement loops. This supports an explainable governance posture rather than a static checklist.
